extra_misconceptions.fact: Two whistle blasts only authorize archers to walk from the waiting line to the shooting line with bows unstrung or arrows in quivers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two whistle blasts on an archery range signal archers on the shooting line to nock an arrow and begin shooting immediately.

extra_misconceptions.fact: No archer may ever reach or step across the shooting line until all shooting stops and the three-whistle retrieval command sounds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An arrow dropped just two feet in front of the shooting line can be quickly grabbed if neighboring archers pause their draw.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bending the shaft or gripping the fletching ruins the arrow; brace the target face near the shaft and pull straight back from the point end.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wiggling an arrow up and down while pulling from the fletching end is the easiest way to free a deeply embedded target point.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only one archer may pull arrows from a target at a time while others stand safely behind the target waiting line away from the nock ends.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All archers assigned to the same target bale should pull their arrows simultaneously to clear the range faster for the next end.

extra_socratic_questions: What action must every archer take immediately upon hearing four or more sharp whistle blasts on the range?
Where should your non-pulling hand and your fellow archers be positioned while drawing an embedded arrow from a target mat?
Why is it dangerous to nock an arrow onto your bowstring while straddling the waiting line before the single whistle blast?
Under what condition is an archer permitted to step forward across the shooting line to retrieve a dropped arrow?

extra_misconceptions.fact: On a standard recurve bow, the index feather must point away from the riser so only two hen feathers glide across the arrow rest.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The differently colored index feather should always point inward toward the bow riser window so the archer can see it clearly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon shafts do not take a permanent bend; impacts cause microscopic cracks that can shatter the shaft upon release and injure the hand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon-fiber arrow shafts that bend slightly after hitting a hard target frame can be straightened in a shop vise like aluminum.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oversized flu-flu fletching creates high aerodynamic drag that rapidly slows the arrow so it drops nearby after a missed aerial shot.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Flu-flu arrows use oversized spiral feathers to stabilize the shaft for long-range accuracy beyond one hundred yards in high wind.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A cracked nock can split open under launch acceleration, causing a dry-fire condition that damages the bow limbs and endangers the archer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A hairline crack in a plastic press-fit nock is harmless to shoot as long as the arrow still clicks onto the bowstring serving.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator distinguishes the index vane from the hen vanes when nocking an arrow onto a recurve bow?
Why is it dangerous to shoot a carbon-fiber arrow shaft without first flexing it and checking for surface splinters?
What flight characteristic makes a flu-flu arrow ideal for aerial targets rather than standard 60-yard target bales?
What happens to arrow flight and nock alignment if hot-melt adhesive is overheated on a carbon shaft during point installation?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard recurve draw weight is rated at a 28-inch draw length; pulling shorter or longer changes the actual poundage held on the fingers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A recurve bow stamped with a 25-pound draw weight requires exactly 25 pounds of force regardless of how far back the string is pulled.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Smooth leather tabs and gloves prevent finger nerve injury while providing a low-friction surface for a clean, repeatable string release.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Finger tabs and leather shooting gloves are worn only for comfort and have no effect on how cleanly the bowstring leaves the fingers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mechanical caliper releases are designed to clip onto a braided D-loop on a compound bowstring to prevent premature serving wear and torque.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A mechanical release aid should be clipped directly around a bare Dacron bowstring just beneath the brass nocking bead.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trapped moisture causes mildew and ruins leather; tabs and gloves should be air-dried at room temperature and stored in a dry container.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Storing leather finger tabs and shooting gloves in a sealed, damp plastic bag keeps the leather soft between campout seasons.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms an archer's true draw length from the nocking point at full draw to the pivot point of the grip?
Where should an arm guard be strapped on the bow arm to prevent bowstring slap without restricting wrist or elbow flexion?
What happens to a recurve bow's effective draw weight when an archer with a 30-inch draw pulls a bow rated at 28 inches?
Which equipment accessories must be removed from a recurve riser for the setup to qualify as a true barebow in competition?

extra_misconceptions.fact: In target archery, any arrow shaft that touches or breaks the dividing line between two scoring rings earns the higher ring's point value.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An arrow shaft that touches the line between the red and gold zones on a World Archery target must be scored as the lower red value.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All arrow values must be called out and recorded on the scorecard before anyone touches an arrow or the target face during retrieval.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An archer may pull their arrows from the target butt first and then mark the point values on the scorecard from memory afterward.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The NFAA field target awards five points for the white center spot, four points for the black middle zone, and three for the outer white ring.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A standard black-and-white NFAA field target uses ten scoring rings from one to ten just like the five-color Olympic target face.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Three-dimensional archery uses life-sized foam animal targets placed along wooded trails with vital-zone scoring rings molded into the foam.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Three-dimensional archery competitions require archers to shoot at flat paper animal pictures pinned to standard straw bales at 18 meters.

extra_socratic_questions: What score does an arrow receive on a five-color World Archery target face when its shaft barely touches the dividing line?
Which physical features distinguish an outdoor NFAA field archery course from a standard World Archery target archery layout?
What happens to a score sheet total if an archer confuses the number of arrows in a single end with a complete tournament round?
What point values are awarded for hitting the black ring versus the inner white spot on a standard NFAA outdoor field target?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Releasing a bowstring without an arrow causes a dry fire that transfers all stored limb energy into the bow, often shattering limbs or cams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drawing and releasing a bowstring without an arrow nocked is a safe way to test the draw weight and cam timing of a compound bow.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The nocking point is set one-eighth to one-quarter inch above square so the arrow clears the rest cleanly without porpoising in flight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A brass nocking locator should be crimped dead-level with the arrow rest so the shaft sits at an exact ninety-degree angle to the string.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The step-through method twists one limb and can crack the lamination; always use a cord bow stringer so both limbs flex evenly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stepping a leg between the bow limb and string is the safest way to bend a laminated recurve bow when attaching the top string loop.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bowstring wax belongs only on exposed synthetic string strands to prevent fraying; waxing the center serving makes it tacky and attracts grit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: String wax should be rubbed heavily over the braided nylon center serving to help the arrow nock snap off the bowstring faster.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to string a recurve bow using the step-through method instead of a properly fitted cord bow stringer?
What happens to vertical arrow impact on the target face if the brass nocking point is crimped too low on the center serving?
Which biomechanical benefit does cam let-off provide to a compound archer while holding at full draw and aligning the sight?
